row.description: One sheet row = one animation (E-35). Playback order: frames before loop_start once, loop_start..loop_end repeated loop_count times, the rest once; hidden frames dropped after loop expansion.

animation.description: Animation name this row plays as (row 0 must be 'idle').

fps.description: Playback rate for this row in frames per second.

frames.description: Number of frame columns in this sheet row.

loop_count.description: Times the looped range plays; 1 = no loop.

loop_end.description: Last frame column of the looped range (inclusive).

loop_start.description: First frame column of the looped range (inclusive).

description: Asset manifest v2 (D-30): maps slot keys to imported sprite sheets plus per-row animation metadata. Written only by the editor's import panel and the E-38 migration tool, through the validating writer.

entries.description: One entry per assigned slot key.

^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$.description: One imported sheet: where it lives, its frame grid size, placement offset, and its animation rows.

anchors.description: Optional named handle points on the sheet frame (ESV-1) — art metadata, not frame geometry, so it never changes how a frame is cut, scaled or blitted. All seven declared names are optional; a missing name or a missing anchors block resolves to no offset.

beam_endpoint.description: Beam terminus on the shooter. Declared for a future read-site; inert today. Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

depth_pivot.description: The point the sprite DEPTH-SORTS at — an enemy's feet. The only anchor read at draw-order time rather than by a draw site: when it is authored, engine/render/renderer.py sorts this entry's sprite at the world point this handle sits on instead of at the entity's tile position, so a lower pivot draws in front. It moves NOTHING visually — the blit is unchanged, and offset_x/offset_y remain the way to nudge one. Absent => sorts at the tile position exactly as before. Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

floater_origin.description: Damage/income floater spawn point. Declared for a future read-site; inert today. Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

hp_bar.description: Overhead HP-bar position offset (game/ui/effects.py). Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

impact.description: Where a hit VFX draws on the target. Parsed and exposed; no draw site wired yet. Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

muzzle.description: Where a projectile visually emits from (game/enemies/combat.py). Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

status_icon.description: Status-badge attach point. Declared for a future read-site; inert today. Frame-px point relative to the sprite anchor, same convention as offset_x/offset_y and slice (+x = right, -y = up), measured on the sheet frame at frame resolution, never at draw resolution or a zoom. [x, y].

column.description: Optional master-column window origin: the 0-based master COLUMN this entry cuts from, the horizontal twin of row_start. Entry frame j of row i cuts sheet x = (column * column_width + j) * frame_w. Omitted => 0 => the entry is byte-identical to a pre-column entry, the same 'optional by omission from required' convention slice, tint_overlay and row_start follow. Master sheets only (D2): meaningless on an imported/<slot>.png entry, which has no columns. 0-based like row_start, hence a ceiling of 255.

column_mode.description: Optional declaration of WHO picks this entry's column (D3). 'manual' (or the key absent) => the stored 'column' above wins. Any other value => a live column supplied by the render path wins, falling back to the stored 'column' when the caller supplies none. The engine only ever distinguishes manual from not-manual (D12); it never learns what a season or a colour is — those meanings live in game/ and editor/, and this enum is the only place their names are written down. 'season' => the map's season stepper drives it; 'building_color' => the placed building's chosen colour index drives it.

column_width.description: How many frame-columns one master column spans, INHERITED from the linked master sheet's registry entry (sprites/master_sheets.json). It is a second copy of a registry value and exists only because engine/ never reads the registry from the cut path — the store sees entry.sheet as an opaque relative path. It cannot drift: no slicing value on a sheet may change while any slot links it. Omitted => 0 => column * 0 + frame_col == frame_col => byte-identical resolution for every pre-column entry. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry: 0 is NOT a legal authored value (minimum 1), it is only the in-memory default for an absent key.

frame_h.description: Frame height in pixels this sheet is sliced at.

frame_w.description: Frame width in pixels this sheet is sliced at.

offset_x.description: Horizontal placement nudge in pixels (positive = right).

offset_y.description: Vertical placement nudge in pixels (negative = up).

row_start.description: Optional row window origin: the 0-based SHEET row that this entry's rows[0] (idle) cuts from; entry row i cuts sheet row row_start + i. Exists so many characters stacked in one master spritesheet can each claim their own contiguous rows. Omit for a sheet this entry starts at the top of — omitted ⇒ 0 ⇒ the entry is byte-identical to a pre-window entry, the same convention slice and tint_overlay follow. The window END is NOT stored: it is len(rows), so there is one source of truth. 0-based like hidden/loop_start, hence a ceiling of 255 against rows' 256-count bound.

rows.description: Sheet rows top to bottom; row 0 is the required idle animation (E-35).

sheet.description: Sheet path relative to data/sprites, resolved as a real path (D-31) — NOT derived from the slot key. Normally imported/<slot>.png, the file this slot's own import owns; but a slot may LINK to another slot's sheet (the editor's 'Use Spritesheet…'), so one PNG can back many slots. It may equally live in master/<sheet_id>.png — a MASTER spritesheet registered in sprites/master_sheets.json, shared by many slots, each claiming its own row window via row_start. Anything deleting art must refcount this field first.

slice.description: Optional nine-slice margins in FRAME pixels [left, top, right, bottom]. When a HUD sprite is drawn at a size other than its frame size, corners blit 1:1, edges stretch on one axis and the centre on both. Omit for plain uniform scaling (world sprites ignore it).

tint_overlay.description: Optional render hint: keep drawing the consumer's own flat colour overlay UNDER this art instead of letting the sprite stand alone. Read today only by the game's tile-condition art (data/slots.json 'conditions' category) — a condition slot with no entry at all always draws the overlay, since there is no sprite. Omit for sprite-only.

version.description: Manifest format version; this schema is v2.
